notes.content: The degree programs presuppose seven semesters of high school level mathematics: algebra (2 years), plane geometry (1 year), and trigonometry (1/2 year); solid geometry and physics are desirable. Deficiencies may be made up by proper selection of courses in the lower division. Recommended courses in lower-division supporting fields are one year of computer science, or economic theory, or general physics with calculus. Courses in mathematical computing, mathematics, operations research and statistics are designed to provide quality undergraduate training in the mathematical sciences and to serve the needs of majors in mathematics, the natural and social sciences, and other fields. The degree programs of the Department of Mathematics provide preparation for various careers in the mathematical sciences. The Department also offers Mathematics Concentration in the Liberal Studies B.A. and Mathematics Minor . View information for the Department of Mathematics , including Learning Objectives.

notes.content: About lower division major requirements and recommended courses

Depending on the student's interest and professional objectives, it is strongly recommended for all mathematics majors to complete one of the sequences listed below in Section 2 under STRONGLY RECOMMENDED COURSES. All courses which apply to the major must be completed with a grade of C- or better.
